title: Service worker never installs, so push notifications and offline support cannot work
standards: W3C Service Workers (install failure on rejected cache.addAll)
steps: In Chromium, navigator.serviceWorker.register('/sw.js') → worker state 'redundant', no active registration.
expected: The worker installs, push subscriptions succeed, and an offline page is served when the network is down.
actual: sw.js precaches ['/', '/index.html']; /index.html does not exist in the Next.js app (Vite leftover), so cache.addAll rejects and the install fails. The worker is only registered when a user enables push, and that registration ends 'redundant'. /offline also redirects guests to /login. If fixed as-is, the fetch handler would cache every GET response, including signed-in API data, with no clearing on logout.
impact: 'Enable notifications' (prompted on many pages) cannot deliver web push, so message and order alerts rely on the open tab; no offline fallback despite the readiness scorecard listing it.
fix: Precache only existing URLs (e.g. '/offline', icons, manifest), make /offline public, never cache /api/* or authenticated responses (or clear caches on logout), register the worker on load, and add a Playwright check that the worker reaches 'activated'.
